donnees.titre: [Multiple mechanisms and intervention strategies of monocytes/macrophages in ocular diseases].
donnees.revue: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
donnees.resume: Monocytes/macrophages possess prominent heterogeneity and functional plasticity, and their functional imbalance participates in the initiation and progression of multiple ocular diseases. This review summarizes the roles of monocytes/macrophages in age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, high myopia, uveitis and glaucoma. It particularly elaborates their pathogenic mechanisms involving oxidative stress, inflammatory amplification, blood-retinal barrier disruption and pathological neovascularization, alongside their immunomodulatory and tissue-repairing functions. We also outline intervention strategies targeting monocytes/macrophages, including blocking pro-inflammatory recruitment and signaling pathways, inducing anti-inflammatory polarization, and immune reprogramming, which may offer novel ideas for precision therapy of chronic inflammatory ocular diseases.
